note: ADR-0006 template-owned path boundary. Ownership is resolved by longest matching prefix; a prefix ending in '/' matches a directory subtree, otherwise it matches an exact file. On a tie, user-owned wins (fail-closed: an upgrade never touches a path it isn't sure the template owns). Conservatively excludes apps/ (portal carries user/plugin pages) and infra/environments/ (per-instance config and secrets) for now; that boundary can widen later. services/api/migrations/versions/ is user-owned even though services/api/ is template-owned: Alembic migration files are an append-only, per-instance chain (each instance accumulates its own, chained by down_revision), so syncing them from the template breaks the instance's revision graph. It stays user-owned — the three-way merge must never rewrite an applied migration — but as of issue #198 `biffo core upgrade` runs a separate *additive* carry for it: new core migrations absent from the instance are appended, re-chained onto the instance's current head at upgrade time (and given a deterministic core_<hash> revision id if the template's own id is already taken in that instance), with the resulting chain validated for a single head before the PR is opened. Existing instance migrations are never modified, re-chained, or deleted. See cli/src/lib/core-migrations.ts. The migration framework itself (migrations/env.py, script.py.mako) stays template-owned. services/_plugins/ is template-owned even though services/ is user-owned: it is the carve-out that gives *first-party* plugins a distribution mechanism (issue #243). A plugin shipped in the template (e.g. orchestrator) previously sat directly under the user-owned services/, so `biffo core upgrade` fail-closed on it and the only channel left was manual PR copy-in — which is the absence of a mechanism, and let every instance's copy drift silently. Longest-prefix-wins resolves services/_plugins/ ahead of services/, exactly as services/api/ already does, so the underscore prefix (matching the existing services/_template/ convention, and un-collidable with a kebab-case plugin name per registry-schema.json) is what declares ownership: a plugin under services/_plugins/ is the template's to maintain and is carried by every upgrade, while a third-party plugin installed into services/<name>/ stays the instance's and is never overwritten. Discovery (services/api/src/api/plugins.py) globs both locations, so the split is an ownership boundary only, never a runtime one. docs/ADR/ is user-owned: the template's ADRs are seeded once at `biffo init` as a starting point, but an instance's ADRs are its own decision record and legitimately diverge from the Biffo standard over time — force-syncing them on every core upgrade collides an instance's own ADR numbers with the template's and rewrites its history. Excluded from the sync flow for that reason; new template ADRs are announced in release notes rather than pushed into instances. core.version is deliberately absent from both lists (so it is user-owned by fail-closed default and never synced): it is the version the *template emits*, its own source of truth, while the version an instance *received* is recorded in the userOwned biffo.core.json — which already wins on every read (cli/src/lib/core-version.ts), leaving the inherited core.version as a mere fallback. Syncing core.version into an instance therefore cannot improve any lookup; it can only overwrite whatever the instance keeps there (one instance repurposed it as its own app release lineage, which an upgrade would regress).
